name: Sugar sculpture
summary: A table piece that a cook models from sugar paste, marzipan and pastry in the shape of a building or a beast. It shows the wealth and skill of the host.
how: Boil sugar to the stage that suits the piece and cast or model it in a mould.
Build the frame of the piece from pastry, wire or wood, and fix the sugar parts to it.
Set the piece at the centre of the table, and bring it in at the end of a service.

origin.note: Late medieval feasts put an edible figure of sugar or paste, a subtlety, on the table between the services.

adoptions.via: Venetian and Roman cooks and sugar workers made large sculptures for the banquets of cardinals and popes.
Carême published his designs for the pièce montée in Le Pâtissier pittoresque.
